name: Shobak
title: David's Warrior and Commander
summary: Shobak (also known as Shophach) was the commander of Hadadezer, king of Zobah. He led the Aramean army against Israel but was defeated by King David in a decisive battle. His defeat helped consolidate David's rule over the region.

keyEvents.title: Aramean Mobilization
keyEvents.description: After David had defeated the Arameans for the first time, Hadadezer gathered new forces from beyond the Euphrates, and Shobak led them as commander-in-chief.

keyEvents.title: Shobak's Campaign Against Israel
keyEvents.description: Shobak led the Aramean army to Helam to fight against Israel, in an attempt to help the Ammonites and restore Aramean dominance.

keyEvents.title: David's Victory at Helam
keyEvents.description: David gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan to meet Shobak's army at Helam. In the ensuing battle, the Arameans were completely defeated.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Shobak
keyEvents.description: Sobak was wounded in the battle and died, which led to the collapse of Aramean resistance and their vassal kings submitting to David.

keyEvents.title: The Submission of the Arameans
keyEvents.description: After Sobak's defeat and death, all Hadadezer's vassals made peace with Israel and came under their rule. The Arameans no longer dared to help the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: The Parallel Account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The same event is described in 1 Chronicles, where the commander is called Shophach. The account confirms David's decisive victory over the Aramean coalition.
